questions.q: Which service does the Ops report query, and against which table?
options: Redshift, against analytics.fact_orders
Athena, directly against northfield_catalog.northfield_orders_curated
Glue, by re-running the ETL job interactively
DynamoDB, against a cached summary table
questions.explain: The Ops report runs as a direct Athena query over the curated catalog table, with no Redshift involved.

questions.q: Who was the original stakeholder this reporting pattern traces back to?
options: Finance, from the Beginner tier
Ops, who ran ad hoc Athena queries against the raw zone in the Beginner project
A brand-new stakeholder never mentioned before
The Redshift database administrator
questions.explain: Ops was the Beginner capstone's original stakeholder, running ad hoc Athena queries before any ETL or warehouse existed.

questions.q: What is the key relationship between the data Finance's report (Lesson 9) and Ops's report (this lesson) each query?
options: They are two separate datasets that happen to produce similar numbers
They are the exact same curated dataset, written by the same Glue ETL job, reached through two different query paths
Ops's data is a day older than Finance's data
There is no relationship; they come from unrelated pipelines
questions.explain: Both reports read from data produced by the same northfield-orders-etl job — Finance via Redshift, Ops directly via Athena over the curated S3 zone.

questions.q: Why isn't Ops simply routed through Redshift as well, given that Spectrum (Lesson 7) could already reach the same data?
options: Redshift cannot physically read Parquet files
It's against AWS policy to query the same data from two services
A single-table, no-join query doesn't need warehouse machinery, and routing it through Redshift anyway adds unnecessary cost and complexity
Athena is being deprecated after this lesson
questions.explain: The right query path depends on the shape of the report; a light single-table query is exactly what Athena already handles well.

questions.q: What does the Ops report's query compute per region?
options: Revenue by product category only
Units sold, number of distinct orders, and average order value
A list of every individual order line item
The Glue ETL job's run duration
questions.explain: The query sums quantity, counts distinct orders, and divides total order value by order count to get avg_order_value, grouped by region.
